title: Rabbi Tavla
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He was a Babylonian, Rav’s student, as in Shabbat 101a, where he asked Rav; Tavla reports “Rav said,” Bava Metzia 94a; in Jerusalem Talmud Eruvin 8:6, Rabbi Avlai in the name of Rav; in Temurah 25a he said to Rabbi Elazar, “Except for that, for Rav said.” In Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 6:4: Rabbi Yaakov bar Acha, Rabbi Tavlai, Chanin bar Ba in the name of Rav.

Hyman suggests that apparently he went up to the Land of Israel to receive ordination, and therefore he is almost always called Rabbi Tavla; but he was not there long, for in Rav Nachman’s days we find him in Babylonia. His place was near Rav Nachman, and he was the judge there, as in Bava Batra 111a: Rabbi Tavla acted according to Rabbi Zekharyah ben HaKatzav. Rav Nachman said to him: “What is this?” He said to him: “But Rabbi Chinena bar Shelamyah said in Rav’s name: The halakhah follows Rabbi Zekharyah ben HaKatzav.” Rav Nachman said to him: “Go retract, or else I will excommunicate you.” In Chullin 132b: Rabbi Tavla’s host was a Kohen … he said to him, “Go join with Israelite butchers” … Rav Nachman held him liable … the butcher said to him, “But Rabbi Tavla exempted me” … Rabbi Tavla went before Rav Nachman, who said to him, “Why did the Master do so?” etc. In Eruvin 102a: “Rabbi Avla came to Mechoza and saw one,” etc. In Eruvin 75a: “Rav Yosef said: This is what I heard from Rabbi Tavla, who said ‘gentile, gentile’ twice, and I did not know what he said.” In Sanhedrin 28b: “Rabbi Tanchum said that Rabbi Tavla said that Rabbi Beruna said that Rav said.” In Menachot 75a, Rav Nachman bar Rav Chisda expounded in the name of Rabbi Tavla. He is mentioned in Jerusalem Talmud Gittin 4:6: he bought a slave and stipulated with the master (if he wanted to return his money to him by such-and-such a time, he would return the slave to him).

notes.text: Tavla reports Rav; the draft’s isolated Rav said lost that nesting. The supplied source writes both RavTavla and RabbiTavla and the variants Avlai/Avla/Tavlai, which remain distinct. His ordination and local judgeship are Hyman’s inferences, not external identity proof.

The consulted Bava Batra 111a literally threatens to remove Chinena bar Shelamya from Tavla’s ears; directly consulted Rashbam explicitly glosses this as I will excommunicate you. Thus Hyman’s excommunication wording has a consulted interpretive basis. Chullin 132b has the host priest’s butcher partnership, patran, and the ensuing Tavla/Nachman dispute; the body’s me rendering is retained beside that plural-form witness. Rav/Rabbi, Avlai/Avla/Tavlai, ordination and local judgeship remain separately qualified.
